$comment: Machine-readable 'what is wrong with the version you are pinned to'.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The consumers table in CLAUDE.md is hand-maintained and has
been wrong twice — most recently claiming leanwise-ai was on #v0.8.1 when it was on
#v1.1.8, eighteen tags of drift that did not exist, on the flagship consumer, in the
table anyone reasons from when judging whether a change is safe to ship.
A consumer cannot see any of this from inside their own repo: their installed tree is
self-consistent and gives no signal that a later release fixed something they are
living with. `lw-doctor` reads the version they have LOCALLY and fetches this file
from the repo TIP — the newest release is the only thing that knows what is wrong
Every `count` here is MEASURED by a named gate, not estimated, and `verifiedAgainst`
records the commit it was measured at. lw-doctor re-derives the counts for the
current tree and fails if an advisory has gone stale — an advisory nobody re-checks
is the same hand-maintained fact this file replaces.

advisories.title: Avatar, EmptyState, Tabs, Pagination and Icon are drawn only by product.css — so a marketing page renders them unstyled
advisories.detail: The README tells a marketing site to load tokens + base + marketing and to drop product.css, and from 1.3.0 that was supposed to be complete. It was not. `.lw-avatar` is rendered by `Byline`, which is rendered by `ArticleCard` — both MARKETING components — and `.lw-icon` is the entire layout contract for the icon set, which `SiteFooter`, `AnnounceBar`, `FeatureGrid`, `PlanCard`, `CompareTable`, `Steps`, `EmptyState`, `Disclosure`, `NavToggle` and `Button` all reach through. `Tabs`, `Pagination` and `EmptyState` are the package's own documented article-index recipe. All five were in the app-surface layer, so composing the recipe as written produced a 0x0 avatar, an unstyled tab strip and page buttons, a centred paragraph where the empty state should be, and every icon on the baseline growing its line box. The flagship consumer worked around it by importing product.css through a `?url` side-channel on two public routes: ~24 KB gzip of app-surface rules on pages that render none of it. If you are pinned below 1.3.1 and load base + marketing only, check any page carrying a byline, a footer icon, a category filter or a paginated index.
advisories.countMeans: rules in product.css whose selector leads with one of the five components' own classes

advisories.title: User-visible English strings are baked into the components and cannot be replaced
advisories.detail: A component library must not hold display text, and this one held a great deal of it. `ArticleCard` emitted the literal `"N min read"`; `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `Toast` hardcoded `Close`/`Dismiss` as both aria-label and tooltip; `ThemeToggle` hardcoded Light/Dark/Auto and its radiogroup name; `RichText`'s ten toolbar buttons carried English accessible names the `tools` prop could only filter, never rename; `DiffReview` held nine words in the accept/reject flow; `Pagination` built "1-25 of 1,284" and every button's accessible name in English; `ActivityFeed` produced Today/Yesterday/This week/Earlier and "3h ago"; `Stepper`, `ToolCall`, `Field`, `BottomNav` and `DiffReview` wrote English into `.lw-sr-only` spans. None of it was reachable by a prop, so a bilingual site rendered English inside its Vietnamese pages with no way to intervene short of forking the component. Every one is now a prop whose default is the previous English string, so the upgrade is additive: `readMinutes` is the single deprecation and it still works, warning once, until v2.0.0.
advisories.countMeans: literal-string aria-label / title / placeholder / alt attributes in components/**/*.jsx — the mechanically countable half of the defect; the full audit found ~70 user-visible literals including rendered text and sr-only words

advisories.title: Every React specimen card rendered blank — so check:a11y and check:visual measured nothing
advisories.detail: esbuild's `jsx` API option is only a DEFAULT: a reachable tsconfig.json overrides it per file, and v1.2.0 added one carrying "jsx": "react-jsx" (correct for tsc, fatal for the browser bundle). Every component in _ds_bundle.js therefore emitted react/jsx-runtime imports and threw `TypeError: import_jsx_runtime.jsx is not a function`, so all 26 React-mounting cards painted their prose and none of their components. check:a11y's guard was `document.body.innerText.length > 0`, which the prose satisfied, and check:visual compared two equally blank plates — so both browser gates reported green across v1.2.0 and v1.2.1 while inspecting nothing. Fixed with `tsconfigRaw: { compilerOptions: {} }` in tools/lw-bundle.mjs; the guard was rebuilt in the same release to fail on an uncaught page error and on any empty React root. The four .lw-btn-link contrast failures the repaired cards immediately exposed were real and are fixed in 1.3.0 too. If you are pinned below 1.3.0, treat any a11y or visual result this package published for its React components as unmeasured.
advisories.countMeans: specimen cards that mount a React root, i.e. that rendered blank

advisories.title: No component declares "use client" — App Router server components throw
advisories.detail: The package shipped zero "use client" directives, so <Combobox>, <DataGrid>, <Dialog>, <Popover>, <Menu> and useTheme() all throw when an App Router page renders them from a server component — the default for every page in every Next app since 2023.

advisories.title: dist/ was never built for any consumer
advisories.detail: prepublishOnly was the only build hook and a git install runs no lifecycle script, so every consumer got raw .jsx and had to put the package inside babel-loader's include. dist/ is committed from 1.2.0.

advisories.title: The lw-token-lint bin is absent in a pnpm install
advisories.detail: `files` used a "!templates/_tooling" exclusion plus a re-include, a pattern npm honours and pnpm does not. A consumer's CI therefore ran no token lint at all, silently. The gates moved to tools/ in 1.2.0 and need no exclusion.

advisories.title: IconName lists 46 of the 78 real glyphs
advisories.detail: The union was hand-maintained, so passing a name the component renders perfectly well — "sidebar", "filter", "send", "copy" and 28 others — was a type error. It is generated from Icon.jsx from 1.2.0.

advisories.title: Every .d.ts uses the bare JSX.Element namespace React 19 removed
advisories.detail: 72 declarations reference `JSX.Element`, which does not resolve under @types/react@19 — so a React 19 consumer with skipLibCheck:false cannot typecheck. There was no tsconfig in the package, so tsc had never run over its own declarations.

advisories.title: base.css carries bare-element rules that beat every Tailwind utility
advisories.detail: Nine un-layered element rules — `button { background:none; border:0; padding:0 }` among them — made base.css unimportable by a Tailwind app, despite the README telling exactly those apps to import it. Split into reset.css in 1.2.0.

advisories.title: No Tailwind v4 artifact — a v4 app has to hand-write the whole bridge
advisories.detail: tailwind-preset.cjs is v3-only. A v4 consumer got no `bg-cta`, no `text-h1`, no `shadow-focus` and no keyframes unless it wrote them itself; tss-app wrote ~600 lines and still lost the fontSize roles, all four backgroundImage surfaces, both durations, the container and every animation. theme.css ships from 1.2.0.
advisories.countMeans: names now offered identically to v3 and v4
